title: Generalized-Maxwell relaxation and dynamic spectrum
purpose: Verify the reusable material-point and signal-processing foundation for linear viscoelastic dynamics without presenting it as a global viscoelastic finite-element solve.
physics: Small-strain thermorheologically simple linear viscoelastic relaxation

execution.evidence: Analytical instantaneous and equilibrium modulus limits, complex storage/loss response, exact branch update and viscous dissipation, temperature-shift direction, positive fixed-spectrum recovery, one-sided FFT amplitude, spectral-ratio FRF, and logarithmic decrement are automated.

observables: Relaxation modulus at zero and long time.
Storage modulus, loss modulus, and loss factor versus angular frequency.
Algorithmic modulus, overstress, and non-negative viscous dissipation for an exact material-point update.
Recovered positive Prony coefficients for a declared relaxation-time spectrum.
FFT amplitude/frequency, FRF phase/amplitude, and free-decay damping quantities.
acceptance: Standard-linear-solid time and frequency limits must match their analytical values.
The exact linear-increment update and integrated branch dissipation must match their closed forms.
The fixed-spectrum fit must recover a synthetic positive two-branch reference to relative RMS error below 1e-12.
Unexcited FRF bins must remain explicitly invalid rather than producing finite high-gain artifacts.
Structured result conversion must retain frequency axes, units, and validity evidence.

quantities.name: instantaneous_modulus
quantities.description: Standard linear solid with equilibrium modulus 2 and one relaxing branch of modulus 8.

quantities.name: storage_modulus_at_omega_tau_one
quantities.description: At omega tau = 1, the relaxing branch contributes half its modulus to storage.

quantities.name: loss_modulus_at_omega_tau_one
quantities.description: At omega tau = 1, the relaxing branch contributes half its modulus to loss.

limitations: This benchmark is material-point and post-processing evidence, not global finite-element viscoelastic validation.
Relaxation times are user-declared; automatic spectrum selection and uncertainty inference are outside this contract.
Nonlinear viscoelasticity, physical aging, complex modes, and direct harmonic finite-element assembly are not verified here.
